content.value_statement: Next.js App Router work can be hard to structure across server, client, and routing boundaries. This skill provides practical patterns for data fetching, streaming, Server Actions, route handlers, metadata, and caching.
actual_capabilities: Explains App Router file conventions for layouts, pages, loading states, errors, route handlers, and metadata.
Provides Server Component and Client Component patterns with data fetching boundaries.
Shows Server Actions for mutations, redirects, cache invalidation, and progressive enhancement.
Demonstrates parallel routes, intercepting modal routes, streaming with Suspense, and loading fallbacks.
Documents fetch caching options, tag revalidation, path revalidation, and metadata generation.
limitations: Does not replace official Next.js documentation for version-specific API changes.
Example code may need authentication, validation, and error handling before production use.
Assumes a React and TypeScript project that already uses the App Router.
Does not install dependencies or run a live Next.js project by itself.

use_cases.title: Plan a New App Router Project
use_cases.description: Choose layouts, pages, loading states, route handlers, and metadata for a new feature before implementation.

use_cases.title: Modernize Pages Router Features
use_cases.description: Map existing pages, API routes, and client data fetching to App Router patterns with clear migration steps.

use_cases.title: Review Rendering and Caching Choices
use_cases.description: Compare Server Components, streaming, revalidation, and tag-based cache invalidation for a feature plan.

prompt_templates.title: Map the App Router Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the App Router file structure for my Next.js feature. Include layouts, pages, loading states, error states, and route handlers where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Page to Server Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature plan and suggest which parts should be Server Components, Client Components, or Server Actions. Explain the data flow and boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Streaming and Caching
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced performance planning for slow data sources.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Next.js App Router page with Suspense streaming, loading fallbacks, fetch caching, and revalidation. Include tradeoffs for each choice.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an App Router Feature Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my App Router feature design for routing, data fetching, cache invalidation, metadata, validation, authorization, and production readiness.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to structure a product listing page with filters.
output: Recommends a server-rendered page that reads search parameters.
Places product data fetching near the product list.
Adds a Suspense boundary for slow list updates.
Uses tag-based cache invalidation for product changes.

output_examples.input: A team wants a photo detail modal that also supports direct links.
output: Suggests an intercepting route for modal navigation.
Keeps a full detail page for direct URLs and refreshes.
Uses a shared detail component to avoid duplicated behavior.

output_examples.input: A lead reviews a product mutation workflow before launch.
output: Checks whether Server Actions or route handlers are the better fit.
Calls out validation, authorization, error handling, and cache revalidation.
Identifies the user-visible loading and failure states.

best_practices: Start with Server Components and add Client Components only for browser state or events.
Place Suspense boundaries around slow data sections so the page can stream useful content early.
Add validation, authorization, and clear error states before using examples in production.
anti_patterns: Moving all data fetching into Client Components without a clear browser need.
Using Server Actions or route handlers without validating inputs and user permissions.
Adding many nested layouts when simple route groups would keep the tree easier to maintain.

faq.question: What Next.js versions does this target?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js 14 and newer App Router concepts, including Server Components, Server Actions, and route handlers.

faq.question: Can it help migrate from Pages Router?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help map pages, API routes, and data fetching patterns to App Router equivalents.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and implementation guidance that must be adapted to a real project.

faq.question: Does it cover Server Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for mutations, redirects, cache revalidation, and progressive enhancement.

faq.question: Are the examples production ready?
faq.answer: They are starting patterns. Add authentication, authorization, validation, logging, and project-specific error handling.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: Claude, Codex, and Claude Code can use the skill content through compatible skill workflows.
